theme: Atomic details: counter, memory ordering and compare and exchange

terms.definition: A number kept in an atomic type that many tasks can add to safely.
terms.example: An atomic counter is enough for simple stats.

terms.definition: A setting on an atomic call that says how strictly other threads must see its changes.
terms.example: Pick the weakest memory ordering that is still correct.
terms.code:
import Synchronization
let flag = Atomic<Bool>(false)
flag.store(true, ordering: .releasing)
print(flag.load(ordering: .acquiring))

terms.definition: An atomic step that changes a value only if it still equals the one you expected.
terms.example: Use compare and exchange to claim the job once.

video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about counting across threads, how strictly changes are seen and conditional updates: Atomic Counter, Memory Ordering & Compare and Exchange, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Atomic Counter - A number kept in an atomic type that many tasks can add to safely.
Memory Ordering - A setting on an atomic call that says how strictly other threads must see its changes.
Compare and Exchange - An atomic step that changes a value only if it still equals the one you expected.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Atomic Counter, Memory Ordering & Compare and Exchange in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Atomic Counter, Memory Ordering, Compare and Exchange 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Atomic Counter - A number kept in an atomic type that many tasks can add to safely.
한국어: Atomic Counter: 여러 태스크가 안전하게 더할 수 있도록 원자 타입에 담아 둔 숫자

Memory Ordering - A setting on an atomic call that says how strictly other threads must see its changes.
한국어: Memory Ordering: 원자 연산의 변경 사항을 다른 스레드가 얼마나 엄격하게 보아야 하는지 정하는 설정

Compare and Exchange - An atomic step that changes a value only if it still equals the one you expected.
한국어: Compare and Exchange: 값이 기대한 값과 여전히 같을 때만 바꾸는 원자 연산

landscape.hook: Can you explain Atomic Counter, Memory Ordering and Compare and Exchange in English?

dialogue.title: What does ordering mean?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I made an atomic counter for our stats, but every call asks for `ordering`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is the memory ordering. It says how strictly other threads must see your change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I used `.relaxed` everywhere. Is that wrong?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For a plain atomic counter, relaxed is fine. Nothing else depends on the number.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And when is it not fine?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: When a flag tells another thread that data is ready. Then you need a stronger memory ordering.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I see. Now I need to claim a job only once.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use compare and exchange. It changes the value only if it still equals what you expected.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So in my code, `exchanged` tells me if I won?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. If two threads try, only one gets true.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. An atomic counter, careful memory ordering and compare and exchange.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Keep the weakest memory ordering that is correct.
An atomic counter is enough for simple stats.
